deities: Burhiya Mai (the Goddess as the 'old mother'; a form of Durga/Shakti)
festivals: Saturdays (heavy weekly crowds; offerings of saris, fruits and flowers)

history.summary: Locally famous temple of the goddess Burhiya Mai on the east-northern portion of Gandhi Maidan in Siwan town. It is believed to fulfil devotees' wishes, and Saturdays see especially large crowds with offerings of saris, fruits and flowers. CONFLICT (verify): a seawatersports.com aggregator page describes a 'Burhiya Mai Temple' in Patna district, which appears to be a different or misattributed entry; the Siwan temple's location is corroborated by indiastatdistricts and mysiwan.com. UNVERIFIED: no reliable source documents the temple's founding date or dynasty.

name: Burhiya Mai Temple
town_description: Siwan is the district headquarters of Siwan district in northwestern Bihar, set on the banks of the Daha river. It is a regional commercial and administrative hub, and the gateway to nearby Ziradei, the birthplace of India's first president Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and to Ashiana, the preserved home of freedom fighter Maulana Mazharul Haq. The town has a subtropical climate with hot summers and mild winters.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~140 km) (verify)
travel.railway: Siwan Junction railway station (in town; the temple is on Gandhi Maidan Rd near the town centre)
travel.road: Well connected by road; NH-227A and state highways link Siwan to Chhapra, Gopalganj and Gorakhpur

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Saturdays are the peak weekly day
